posing_source.locator: Section 4.4, page 20; arXiv v3 main.tex lines 735-744

lean.coverage: Negation of the universal isotropic-line-family equality claim, using the fixed IIZ perp, positive contextuality degree at most 12, and hexagon intersection at least 15.

written_proofs: Exact degree 12 for every three-qubit perp by linear sections and signed Clifford transport.
Exact intersection 15 with every three-regular isotropic line family on all 63 points.
Arbitrary-pole degree identity d(C_p^(n)) = 4 d(L_(n-1)) for every n >= 2 and every nonzero p; in particular every four-qubit perp has degree 252 using d(L_3) = 63.
Characterization of optimal IIZ-perp assignments by their 16 linear sections and 15 pole lines.
Degree-1 19-line counterexample with intersection at least 3.
Upper-bound inequality from a satisfying assignment on the complement.
finite_checks: 315 three-qubit isotropic lines and their signs by matrix products and binary phase exponents.
15 two-qubit lines, ten parity grids, and all 32768 two-qubit assignments.
31 perp points, 75 perp lines, 12 negative lines, 16 linear sections, and fourfold section coverage.
A classical coordinate model with 63 lines and intersection 15 at every one of 63 poles.
Canonical negative-line counts for all 63 three-qubit poles, including 12 at IIZ and 24 at YYY.
The 19-line union, its single negative line, and the six-line parity contradiction.
